name: Victron Energy Bluesolar Mono 130W
notes: Technology: monocrystalline cells (36 cells at 130 W and 150 W, 39 at 190 W), monofacial, high-transmission tempered glass in an anodised aluminium frame with MC4 leads. Pros: a well-known leisure and marine panel with a 12 V-class Vmp that suits small 12/24 V MPPT chargers; good low-light performance; 1000 V system rating and a 25-year output warranty. Cons: heavy for its output compared with a flexible panel, too low-voltage for a grid-tied string inverter, and a Pmax temperature coefficient (-0.45 %/°C) at the weak end of the range, so it loses more power when hot. Notable: the 150 W uses the same 1485 x 668 mm frame as the 190 W, so it is much less efficient; Victron's current datasheet states 18.9 % for it, but the power and size give 15.1 %, which is the figure used here.
